Purpose

This workbook restates our current understanding of the CBC estimating & pricing process as a structured requirements matrix, so the estimating team can confirm each item, correct anything wrong, and answer the open questions. Nothing here is final until confirmed. Once confirmed, it becomes the agreed basis for the estimating-and-pricing copilot build.
The tabs
1.  Requirements Matrix  —  Every requirement grouped into Epics, with our Understanding, Assumptions, and Questions. Two columns are for YOU: 'Confirmation' and 'Client Response / Corrections'.
2.  Process Flow  —  End-to-end current-state flow, Phase 0 (Intake) to Phase 6 (Deliver), to confirm step by step.
3.  Product & Scope Confirmation  —  Every product category & manufacturer CBC lists publicly, cross-checked against the workshop. Tell us which ones estimating actually quotes.
4.  Business Case & Metrics  —  The 'why' and the numbers: strategic objectives, baseline, targets, and success criteria for leadership to set. (New in v1.1.)
5.  Assumptions & Dependencies  —  What must be true — and what CBC must provide — for the build to succeed. (New in v1.1.)
6.  Open Items  —  The specific answers we still need (data, sheets, values, thresholds).
How to fill it in
•  Yellow cells are for you — use the drop-downs, or type freely in the notes/response columns.
•  Confirmation options: Accurate / Needs Correction / Pending Review. If 'Needs Correction', say what's wrong in the response column.
•  Answer the Questions in the same row's response column, and the Open Items on the last tab.
Guiding principle
The estimator stays in control of every quote. The copilot drafts, sources, and calculates — it does not send. Its job is to remove manual re-keying and lookup, not to replace estimating judgment.

Bid alternates & addenda

Commercial bids commonly carry bid alternates (Alternate 1, 2…) and are revised mid-bid by addenda that change scope, products, or counts. The estimate must track a base bid plus alternates and absorb addendum revisions without losing prior work.
Alternates and addenda occur on a meaningful share of bids and must be first-class, not exceptions.

4. Quote Calculation Logic
Three manual inputs; rest computed

The quote workbook is a calculator. Only three cells are human per line: Quantity (take-off), Our Cost (P21 / vendor), and Margin (by product type). Everything to the right is computed: Sale $ EA = Cost / (1 - margin); Unit = Sale $ EA; Ext = Unit x Qty; Sub-total = Sale $ EA x Qty; Grand total = SUM(subtotals); Total weight = Unit weight x Qty.
Unit weight is often 0 / unpopulated, so weight-based freight is usually not computed.
Must
Are Quantity, Our Cost, and Margin the only manual inputs? Is unit weight ever reliably populated for freight?
Accurate (corrected)
[Confirmed — estimator session 14 Jul] All quote-calc formulas validated EXCEPT 'unit weight' — legacy from truck-loading years ago; not used, remove it. Everything else accurate.
5. Pricing & Cost Rules
Margin framework by product type

Margin applied by division as a divisor; framework stable ~14 years. Bands: Commodity 27% (/0.73); Restroom partitions 35% (/0.65); Specialty e.g. laminated doors 40% (/0.60); Custom-built via outside fabricator 25% (/0.75). Bands are defaults the estimator adjusts by experience.
Lead time & sourcing move the margin; genuinely custom first-builds need a hand-entered margin.
Must
Are the four bands and divisors correct? What product types beyond these four make up the rest (the full margin sheet, ~95% coverage)? (Open item 2.)
Accurate (corrected)

[Confirmed — estimator session 14 Jul] Top-10 vendors; use the margins sheet provided. Margin is OVERRIDABLE on essentially every quote based on sourcing (e.g., Wendy's special margin; if bought via Banner/SecLock at higher cost the margin drops). Accessory band derives to ~56% from data (was 35%). Margin-approval routing = OUT of scope for now (no deviation today) — future.
Cost sourcing from P21

For regularly-bought items, cost = the LAST purchase-order price (from purchase history or the cost screen). Do NOT trust P21's 'supplier list / supplier cost' fields — purchasing doesn't reliably update them. Freshness: cost older than ~6–8 months is unreliable; 3–4 years must be discarded. Special-priced items already carry their cost in P21.
Read-only access to P21 is sufficient for this workstream (no write-back).
Must
Is the last-PO logic and ~6–8 month freshness rule correct? Cost entry mechanic — typed from the P21 screen, or pasted from a P21 export? (Open item 4.)
Accurate

[Confirmed — estimator session 14 Jul] P21 last-PO used often for one-offs. Three cost paths: (1) last-PO if sold <1 yr & no price increase (9/10 correct); (2) else look up Banner/SecLock (Allegion, not bought direct); (3) else mfr website for never-sold direct parts. P21 integration to be investigated — risk: P21 item IDs often differ from mfr part numbers, and 'semi/custom items' won't match. Manual entry must always be available.
Supplier list price x multiplier

When an item isn't on special pricing, cost = manufacturer list price x a customer-specific multiplier (CBC's discount tier). Hager (~75% of volume) has custom-negotiated pricing — e.g. a 3500-series storeroom lock lists $256.31, a '50 & 42' discount ≈ 0.29 multiplier → cost ≈ $74. World Dryer example: HP is Level-3 (0.339); the vendor sheet pre-computes net. MAP is NOT cost. Price changes arrive as dated memos with a protection window.
The multiplier is a per-vendor account attribute (a tier), not a per-item value; the model is near-universal.
Must
Is the list x multiplier method + tier / MAP / price-memo read correct? Can we get the current multiplier sheets & tiers for all active vendors? (Open item 3.)
Accurate

[Confirmed — estimator session 14 Jul] List x multiplier confirmed. NOTE manual ADDERS not shown cleanly in the price book (electrification, non-removable-pin hinges, premium/lead-time finishes) must be added on top of the base price. Beyond P21 and list x multiplier, we understand some items — large, special, non-stock, or first-time — are priced by requesting a live quote (RFQ) from the vendor or fabricator. This is a distinct third cost route the copilot must accommodate (request out, quote back, cost entered by hand).

There is appetite for a soft control (flag / approve) rather than a hard lock.

Process Flow: Current-State Estimating Process — Start to Finish (Phases 0–6)
Confirm each step reflects how a bid is actually worked. Reading specs & drawings up front is the largest time cost in every bid.
Bid request arrives by email; the bid set is a PDF — sometimes one combined file, sometimes many separate PDFs. Note any bid alternates and the bid-due date at intake.
Bid set (PDF/s); alternates & due date noted

[Confirmed 14 Jul] Bid arrives mostly by email (job workbook + plans/RFP attached); sometimes by phone -> add a 'create new bid request' option. Requests come from the internal initiator in the queue (Kellan/Matt/Rebecca/Tina), not the architect.
Copy the project folder / name, then Save As a new job workbook from a prior job's file; clear the previous job's residual rows.
[Confirmed 14 Jul] Templated mode copies an existing workbook & modifies per RFP (Shanna); Kevin builds one-off from scratch (exceptions McDonald's, Cava). Workbooks password-protected ('estimator').

Identify the Division 8 (doors, frames, hardware) and Division 10 (partitions, accessories, washroom equipment) scope; read the specification — including fire ratings and the hardware-set (HW) schedule — to confirm exactly what is being quoted.
[Confirmed 14 Jul] Scope identified manually from the spec/RFP PDFs — Div 8 doors/frames/hardware + Div 10 specialties + FRP. Fire-rating capture still to confirm (Matrix 7.3).
Review the drawings — manual PDF read or digital take-off — for perimeters, corners, counts, door sizes, handing, and rating.
[Confirmed 14 Jul] Drawings reviewed and taken off manually (Edge / Vu360 viewer).

Where FRP is specified, set drawing scale in Vu360 and capture perimeter (LF), inside corners, outside corners. Vu360 gives geometry only; the estimator converts to material quantities by hand and types them in.
[Confirmed 14 Jul] Vu360 + calculator for FRP wall-panel measurement (Shanna). Geometry->quantity conversion constants still to be provided.

Populate the workbook. Price each line — apply the product-type margin; special-priced items carry cost in P21; others priced from vendor list x multiplier; large/special/non-stock items go to a vendor RFQ. Freight often carried 'TBD'.

[Confirmed 14 Jul] Populate Excel & price. Two paths: Shanna from available data; Kevin manual calc using vendor multiplier sheets + calls for parts not in P21/multiplier. Only Qty/Cost/Margin manual; remove legacy unit-weight.

Price bid alternates as distinct, comparable line groups. When an addendum arrives, reconcile the changed scope/products/counts into the estimate without losing prior work, and re-issue if already sent.
Formal alternates / addenda handling NOT covered in the session — still to confirm.
Reuse similar past jobs for a repeat brand/architect/GC. Handle direct-equal substitutions (ask GC to approve an equal). Raise RFIs for unclear or missing info before finalizing.
[Confirmed 14 Jul] Reuse the closest prior quote (templated mode). Value-engineering: when a specified line isn't available, propose the closest of the top 2-3 brands with a note.

Export to a PDF proposal — doors/frames/hardware grouped by door with subtotals, a separate restroom-accessories block, a freight line (often TBD), and standard commercial terms (HP PO required; 30-day validity). Send via Outlook.

[Confirmed 14 Jul] Export to a PDF proposal and send back to whoever initiated the request in the queue (SALES), NOT a group email; they then deal with the customer. Freight generally omitted at estimate (handled at job stage).
Green = new in v1.1 (alternates & addenda, and rating/handing detail added to intake, scoping & take-off).
